speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding gums, and tiny red spots on your skin. To understand the cause, have you been experiencing easy bruising or bleeding after minor injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae, and easy bruising in a 4-year-old is highly characteristic of thrombocytopenia. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes like leukemia, I need to see the platelet count and a blood smear.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count
REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Smear
